request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every successful change to a sheet is now written to the audit file in the format requested. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**Server**
- The person and claim services write `PERSON_ADDED`, `PERSON_EDITED`, `CLAIM_ADDED` and `CLAIM_EDITED` lines. They use what was actually saved: the trimmed name, the amount with two decimals and the date as `yyyy-mm-dd`.
- Lines are written through a new `Audit.recordOnCommit` method, which only appends once the database change has committed. So a change that is refused or rolled back writes nothing, whichever rule refuses it, including rules added later.

**Signed-in user**
- Until now the server never knew who was signed in, so I had to add that. A small front-end hook (`core/signed-in.ts`, registered in `app.config.ts`) adds an `X-User` header to every request once someone has signed in.
- The four add/edit endpoints now require that header. The name is URL-encoded on the way out and decoded by a small helper, `SignedIn.java`, so names with spaces or accented letters still arrive intact.

One side effect: anything calling those four endpoints directly, without the `X-User` header, will now be rejected. The app's own screens always send it, since they only allow changes after sign-in.
